# PHP2Shell Labs

> PHP2Shell exposure of a public host: a stage (NO PATCH, EXPOSED, HIDDEN, NOT AFFECTED, PROTECTED; NOT PHP and UNREACHABLE without a score), a score 0-100, and the one next step. Free, open source (MIT), no key.

The exposure test makes one ordinary visit to the host you name plus PHP's credit query and compares the advertised PHP version with the fixed releases for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35). The exploit validation is consent-gated: one small posted request and one large chunked request of about 48 MB, judged by the answer; no exploit code is sent. Only test hosts you are allowed to connect to.

## API

- One answer: GET https://php2shell-labs.taptok-test.workers.dev/api/scan?host=example.com
  or POST /api/scan with {"host": "example.com", "validate": false} and `Accept: application/json`.
  Returns {id, url, pdf, cached, result}; result.assessment has stage, score, verdict, nextStep.
- Consent: "validate": true (or &validate=1 on GET) runs the exploit validation. Skipped when nothing answered as PHP.
- Live events: POST /api/scan without that Accept header streams application/x-ndjson
  (start, fingerprint, probe..., validation, assessment, done, result, saved).
- Stored result: GET /api/result/{id} (never changes).
- PDF report: GET /api/report/{id}.pdf (five pages; the first after a quiet spell may take 20 s).
- Human page: https://php2shell-labs.taptok-test.workers.dev/r/{id} (unlisted, Open Graph preview).
- Full description: https://php2shell-labs.taptok-test.workers.dev/openapi.json
- Human documentation: https://php2shell-labs.taptok-test.workers.dev/api

## Limits

- 20 scans per caller address and 6 per host in any hour; 4 validations per caller address in any hour; 429 with Retry-After.
- Exposure results under 24 hours old are answered from cache (cached: true); a consented validation always runs fresh.
- Public hosts on ports 80 and 443 only; private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused.
- CORS open: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

## Reading a result

- no-patch: PHP 5.4 through 8.1, end-of-life branch inside the affected range; only an upgrade removes the flaw.
- exposed: PHP 8.2 through 8.5.11; install the branch's fixed release.
- hidden: PHP runs but hides its version; treated as exposed until known. The validation can place it.
- not-affected: PHP older than 5.4; the vulnerable code does not exist in it.
- protected: a fixed release or newer.
- not-php / unreachable: nothing answered as PHP, or no web server answered; no score.
- Scoring: https://github.com/manteiga-foundation/php2shell-labs/blob/main/docs/scoring.md
